summary: notebook-auto-prune.sh sentinel-key logic drops the ONLY freshly-timestamped section, not the oldest — reproduced 2x live on dev-team.md this tick

payload.mechanism: nso_ts_key() in scripts/agents-flow/lib/notebook-section-direction.sh assigns NSO_SENTINEL_KEY="99999999999999999" (MAX) to any '## ' heading with no parseable timestamp, by design so untimestamped ROLLING sections (e.g. '## Lessons / patterns', '## Known patterns / preferences') never look oldest. But this has an unhandled inverse: when a file mixes rolling untimestamped sections with exactly one dated per-tick section, the dated section is the ONLY one with a real (small) numeric key, so it is ALWAYS the MIN_KEY and is selected as 'oldest' and dropped first by notebook-auto-prune.sh's drop-oldest loop -- even when it was just written this same tool call. Verified live: docs/agent-memory/notebooks/dev-team.md has 3 sections ('## Current state (tick ...)', '## Lessons / patterns', '## Carry-over'); only 'Current state' has a parseable date. Wrote a closeout addendum to 'Current state' via Edit -> hook fired -> entire section deleted (43->32 lines). Retried via full-file Write (different tool, same hook) -> IDENTICAL section deleted again (44->31 lines). 2/2 reproductions, same session, same mechanism.
payload.secondary_gap: the byte-cap trigger for this file is itself borderline-permanent: BYTE_CAP = LINE_CAP(200)*60 = 12000 bytes assumes a 60-bytes/line average, but this fleet's convention (dense single-line bullets, 500-1500 bytes each) blows that budget long before the 200-line cap -- dev-team.md was ~44 lines / ~12.2KB, i.e. over the BYTE axis only, not the LINE axis. Any notebook using this dense-bullet style plus >=1 rolling untimestamped section will hit this same drop-the-freshest bug on its very next dated-section write.
payload.silent_loss_gap: the hook emits a signal on every OTHER path (unparseable, single-section breach, duplicate-heading, direction-defaulted) but NOT on a normal successful drop-oldest cycle -- from the hook's own perspective this is 'working as designed', so nobody is notified a section was actually deleted. Content is recoverable from git history (this file is git-tracked) but only if someone happens to diff it; would be silent for an agent that doesn't check.
recommended_fix_directions: exclude sentinel-keyed (undated/rolling) sections entirely from MIN_KEY eligibility when at least one OTHER section has a real timestamp -- a rolling section being 'immune from ever looking oldest' should not imply a dated section is therefore always 'more oldest' than it; the two predicates need to be decoupled

alternatively/additionally: emit an informational signal (mirroring notebook_tiebreak_direction_defaulted's pattern) any time the drop-oldest loop actually removes a section, naming the file + dropped heading + line span + byte delta, so content loss is always auditable even on the 'working as designed' path
payload.not_yet_fixed_by: distinct mechanism from the FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTO-PRUNE-STALENESS-GUARD backlog row (main.md notebook's occurrence 6 -- a byte-identical single-writer Edit-apply failure with unconfirmed root cause) and from reference_agent_notebook_ordering_convention_not_fleet_uniform (ordering-convention mismatch across the fleet) -- this is a specific, now mechanistically-confirmed sentinel-vs-real-key defect inside the drop-oldest section-selection logic itself, reproducible on a SINGLE file with a SINGLE consistent convention.
payload.recovery_action_taken: did not retry a 3rd write against the same hook path (recurring 2/2 same-mechanism failure -> escalate, don't keep fighting it). Load-bearing facts from the lost section (task_release result, .head reset commit aa6eb95f3, developer agent adfd042ed7610db5d RAW-verify results) remain durably recorded in git commit history and docs/data/orch/orch-state.json regardless of notebook prose loss -- no operational data was actually lost, only the narrative summary.
